chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The Hajj is (performed in) the well-known months'
so whoever determines the performance of the Hajj therein
And the Obligation is the Talbiyya, and the Ish'ar, and the Taqlid
So whoever does that, so he has done the Hajj
and the Hajj is not determined except during these months which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Says are 'the well-known months'
and these are Shawwal, and Dhu al-Qadah, and Dhu al-Hijjah

key_terms.التَّقْلِيدُ: Taqlid: The act of placing the Hajj camel's halter or leading the animal
key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةُ: Talbiyya: The recitation of 'Labbayk' upon entering the state of Ihram
key_terms.الْإِشْعَارُ: Ish'ar: The act of pointing or directing the sacrificial animal
key_terms.ذُو الْحِجَّةِ: Dhu al-Hijjah: The twelfth month of the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.ذُو الْقَعْدَةِ: Dhu al-Qadah: The eleventh month of the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.شَوَّالٌ: Shawwal: The tenth month of the Islamic lunar calendar

ai.seo_question: What are the specific ritual acts that determine the Hajj and which months are considered the well-known months for Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the practical application of Quran 2:197 by defining the specific ritual acts—Talbiyya (verbal declaration), Ish'ar (pointing to the Kaaba), and Taqlid (tying the Ihram garment)—that constitute the formal entry into the state of Ihram for Hajj. It further specifies the 'well-known months' (Ashhur Ma'lumat) as Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, and Dhu al-Hijjah, establishing the temporal window for performing these rites. This narration is significant in Shia jurisprudence for linking the textual definition of the months with the procedural requirements of the pilgrimage.
